violations.description: Use of pull_request_target with checkout of untrusted PR head.
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/auto-label.yml uses pull_request_target and checks out the PR head ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}.
violations.recommendation: Do not check out untrusted PR head code when using pull_request_target.

violations.description: Hardcoded secret in workflow environment block.
violations.recommendation: Remove the hardcoded secret and use GitHub Secrets with ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}.

violations.description: Missing permissions block in security-sensitive workflow.
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/auto-label.yml uses pull_request_target but does not define a permissions block, granting default (often excessive) permissions.
violations.recommendation: Add an explicit permissions block to restrict the GITHUB_TOKEN to the minimum necessary scopes.

violations.description: Untrusted PR event input used in a shell script without sanitization.
violations.evidence: The greeting workflow uses ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} directly in a shell command. An attacker could inject commands into the PR title.
violations.recommendation: Always sanitize or use environment variables to pass PR event data into shell scripts.

violations.evidence: package.json exists but no package-lock.json or similar lockfile is present in the repository.
violations.recommendation: Generate and commit a package-lock.json file.
